label: Physics 11 — Mechanics & Pressure
description: Subjective numericals across the full 5-level hierarchy. Two questions are matched to real handwritten answer sheets, so the AI evaluation on them is a genuine reading rather than noise.

questions.body: A car starts from rest and accelerates uniformly over a time of 5.21 seconds for a distance of 110 m. Determine the acceleration of the car.
questions.rubric: 1 mark: writes s = ut + ½at². 1 mark: substitutes u = 0. 2 marks: correct rearrangement a = 2s/t². 1 mark: correct value 8.10 m/s² with unit.

answerSheets.note: Rearranges v² = u² + 2as and answers a = 10 — correct method, but not this question's data. Verified: the engine scores it 0/5.
Lists formulas then asserts v = 50 + 75 = 125. Incoherent.

questions.body: A car accelerates uniformly from 18 km/h to 72 km/h in 10 s. Find (a) its acceleration and (b) the distance it covers in that time.
questions.rubric: 1 mark: converts both speeds to m/s (5 m/s and 20 m/s). 2 marks: a = (v − u)/t = 1.5 m/s². 2 marks: s = (u + v)t/2 = 125 m.
questions.explanation: Unit conversion first (÷ 3.6), then the two standard relations. a = 1.5 m/s², s = 125 m.

questions.body: A body starts from rest and covers 40 m in 4 s with uniform acceleration. Find its acceleration and its velocity at the end of 4 s.
questions.rubric: 2 marks: s = ½at² → a = 5 m/s². 2 marks: v = at = 20 m/s. 1 mark: units on both answers.

questions.body: A train moving at 20 m/s applies its brakes, producing a uniform retardation of 2 m/s². Find (a) the distance it travels before stopping and (b) the distance it covers during the 5th second of braking.
questions.rubric: 3 marks: v² = u² + 2as with v = 0 → s = 100 m. 2 marks: checks the train is still moving in the 5th second (stops at t = 10 s). 4 marks: sₙ = u + a(2n − 1)/2 = 11 m. 1 mark: units.
questions.sampleAnswer: u = 20 m/s, a = −2 m/s². (a) 0 = 400 − 4s → s = 100 m. (b) The train stops at t = u/|a| = 10 s, so the 5th second is a real interval. s₅ = u + a(2n − 1)/2 = 20 + (−2)(9)/2 = 20 − 9 = 11 m.
questions.explanation: Stopping distance 100 m. Distance in the nth second uses sₙ = u + a(2n − 1)/2, giving 11 m — not to be confused with distance in 5 s.

questions.body: Starting from the equation v² = u² + 2as, obtain an expression for the acceleration a. Hence find a for a body whose velocity changes from 0 to 20 m/s over a distance of 20 m.
questions.rubric: 3 marks: correct rearrangement a = (v² − u²)/2s. 2 marks: substitution giving a = 10 m/s² with unit.
questions.sampleAnswer: v² = u² + 2as → v² − u² = 2as → a = (v² − u²)/(2s). With u = 0, v = 20 m/s, s = 20 m: a = 400/40 = 10 m/s².
questions.explanation: Pure rearrangement followed by one substitution. a = 10 m/s².

answerSheets.note: Rearranges to a = (v² − u²)/2s and states a = 10.

questions.body: A ball thrown vertically upward returns to the thrower's hand after 6 s. Taking g = 10 m/s², find (a) the speed with which it was thrown and (b) the maximum height it reached.
questions.rubric: 2 marks: time of ascent = 3 s. 2 marks: u = gt = 30 m/s. 1 mark: h = u²/2g = 45 m.
questions.sampleAnswer: Total time 6 s, so time to the top = 3 s. At the top v = 0: 0 = u − g(3) → u = 30 m/s. h = u²/2g = 900/20 = 45 m.
questions.explanation: Symmetry of projectile motion: ascent time equals descent time. u = 30 m/s, h = 45 m.

questions.body: A stone is dropped from the top of a tower. It crosses the last 20 m before hitting the ground in 1 s. Taking g = 10 m/s², find the height of the tower.
questions.rubric: 3 marks: sets up ½gT² − ½g(T − 1)² = 20. 4 marks: solves to T = 2.5 s. 3 marks: H = ½gT² = 31.25 m.
questions.sampleAnswer: Let T be the total fall time. Distance in the last second = ½gT² − ½g(T − 1)² = 20. So 5[T² − (T − 1)²] = 20 → 5(2T − 1) = 20 → 2T − 1 = 4 → T = 2.5 s. H = ½ × 10 × 6.25 = 31.25 m.
questions.explanation: The difference of two 'distance fallen' expressions, not a fresh u = 0 fall over the last 20 m. H = 31.25 m.

questions.body: Two trains, 120 m and 80 m long, move on parallel tracks in opposite directions at 20 m/s and 30 m/s. How long do they take to cross each other completely?
questions.rubric: 2 marks: relative speed = 50 m/s for opposite directions. 2 marks: relative displacement = 200 m (sum of lengths). 1 mark: t = 4 s.
questions.sampleAnswer: Opposite directions, so v_rel = 20 + 30 = 50 m/s. To cross completely the relative displacement is 120 + 80 = 200 m. t = 200/50 = 4 s.
questions.explanation: Adding speeds (opposite motion) and lengths (full crossing) are the two marks worth checking. t = 4 s.

questions.body: Rain is falling vertically with a constant speed. A man walking at 10 km/h finds the rain meeting him at 45° to the vertical. Find the speed of the rain and the speed of the rain relative to the man.
questions.rubric: 3 marks: draws/states v_rain,man = v_rain − v_man. 4 marks: tan 45° = v_man/v_rain → v_rain = 10 km/h. 3 marks: relative speed = 10√2 ≈ 14.1 km/h.
questions.sampleAnswer: In the man's frame the rain has a horizontal component equal and opposite to his own velocity. tan 45° = v_man/v_rain → 1 = 10/v_rain → v_rain = 10 km/h. Relative speed = √(10² + 10²) = 10√2 ≈ 14.1 km/h.
questions.explanation: The apparent tilt comes entirely from the observer's own velocity. v_rain = 10 km/h, v_rel = 14.1 km/h.

questions.body: A boat can row at 5 m/s in still water. A river 100 m wide flows at 3 m/s. If the boatman wants to cross by the shortest path, in what direction must he head, and how long does the crossing take?
questions.rubric: 2 marks: heads upstream at angle θ with sin θ = 3/5, i.e. 37° to the normal. 2 marks: effective across-stream speed = √(25 − 9) = 4 m/s. 1 mark: t = 25 s.
questions.sampleAnswer: For zero drift the upstream component must cancel the current: 5 sin θ = 3 → θ = 37° upstream of the line straight across. Across-stream speed = 5 cos θ = 4 m/s. t = 100/4 = 25 s.
questions.explanation: Shortest path means zero drift, not minimum time. t = 25 s heading 37° upstream.

questions.body: Two blocks of masses 4 kg and 6 kg are in contact on a frictionless horizontal surface. A force of 20 N is applied horizontally to the 4 kg block. Find the acceleration of the system and the contact force between the blocks.
questions.rubric: 2 marks: a = F/(m₁ + m₂) = 2 m/s². 2 marks: free-body diagram of the 6 kg block. 1 mark: contact force = 6a = 12 N.
questions.sampleAnswer: a = 20/(4 + 6) = 2 m/s². For the 6 kg block the only horizontal force is the contact force N: N = 6 × 2 = 12 N.
questions.explanation: System first for a, then isolate one block for the internal force. a = 2 m/s², N = 12 N.

questions.body: Masses of 5 kg and 3 kg hang from the two ends of a light inextensible string passing over a frictionless pulley. Taking g = 10 m/s², find (a) the acceleration of the masses, (b) the tension in the string and (c) the force on the pulley.
questions.rubric: 3 marks: two equations of motion, one per mass. 3 marks: a = (m₁ − m₂)g/(m₁ + m₂) = 2.5 m/s². 3 marks: T = 2m₁m₂g/(m₁ + m₂) = 37.5 N. 1 mark: pulley force = 2T = 75 N.
questions.sampleAnswer: For the 5 kg mass: 5g − T = 5a. For the 3 kg mass: T − 3g = 3a. Adding: 2g = 8a → a = 2.5 m/s². T = 3(g + a) = 3 × 12.5 = 37.5 N. Both string segments pull down on the pulley, so the force on it is 2T = 75 N.
questions.explanation: Standard Atwood machine. a = 2.5 m/s², T = 37.5 N, pulley force 75 N (not 8g).

questions.body: A man of mass 60 kg stands on a weighing machine inside a lift. Taking g = 10 m/s², find the reading of the machine (in newtons) when the lift accelerates upward at 2 m/s², and state what it would read if the cable snapped.
questions.rubric: 3 marks: N − mg = ma → N = m(g + a) = 720 N. 2 marks: free fall gives a = −g, so N = 0.
questions.sampleAnswer: Upward acceleration: N − mg = ma → N = 60(10 + 2) = 720 N. In free fall a = g downward, so N = m(g − g) = 0 — the man is weightless.
questions.explanation: Apparent weight is the normal reaction, not mg. 720 N, then 0 N.

questions.body: A 10 kg block rests on a horizontal surface with μs = 0.4 and μk = 0.3. A horizontal force of 30 N is applied. Taking g = 10 m/s², does the block move? Find the frictional force acting on it and its acceleration.
questions.rubric: 2 marks: limiting static friction = μsN = 40 N. 2 marks: 30 N < 40 N so the block stays at rest. 1 mark: friction = 30 N (self-adjusting), a = 0.
questions.sampleAnswer: N = mg = 100 N. Limiting static friction = 0.4 × 100 = 40 N. The applied 30 N is less than this, so the block does not move. Static friction adjusts to exactly 30 N and a = 0. (μk is a distractor — it only applies once sliding starts.)
questions.explanation: The common error is using μk immediately and reporting a non-zero acceleration. f = 30 N, a = 0.

questions.body: A 5 kg block slides down a rough incline of 30° with μk = 0.2. Taking g = 10 m/s², find its acceleration and its speed after sliding 10 m from rest.
questions.rubric: 3 marks: resolves along and normal to the incline. 4 marks: a = g(sin θ − μ cos θ) = 3.27 m/s². 3 marks: v = √(2as) ≈ 8.1 m/s.
questions.sampleAnswer: Along the incline: mg sin θ − μmg cos θ = ma → a = g(sin 30° − 0.2 cos 30°) = 10(0.5 − 0.1732) = 3.27 m/s². From rest over 10 m: v = √(2 × 3.27 × 10) = √65.4 ≈ 8.1 m/s.
questions.explanation: Mass cancels out of the acceleration. a ≈ 3.27 m/s², v ≈ 8.1 m/s.

concepts.name: Work Done by a Variable Force

questions.body: A force F = 3x² N acts on a body along the x-axis. Find the work done in moving the body from x = 0 to x = 2 m.
questions.rubric: 2 marks: writes W = ∫F dx. 2 marks: evaluates ∫₀² 3x² dx = [x³]₀². 1 mark: W = 8 J with unit.
questions.sampleAnswer: W = ∫₀² F dx = ∫₀² 3x² dx = [x³]₀² = 8 − 0 = 8 J.
questions.explanation: A variable force needs the integral, not F × d. W = 8 J.

questions.body: A 2 kg block moving at 10 m/s on a rough horizontal surface comes to rest after travelling 25 m. Taking g = 10 m/s², find the work done by friction, the frictional force and the coefficient of kinetic friction.
questions.rubric: 3 marks: work-energy theorem W = ΔKE = −100 J. 3 marks: f = |W|/s = 4 N. 3 marks: μ = f/mg = 0.2. 1 mark: sign of the work is negative.
questions.sampleAnswer: Initial KE = ½ × 2 × 100 = 100 J, final KE = 0. By the work-energy theorem the work done by friction = −100 J. Since W = −f·s, f = 100/25 = 4 N. μk = f/mg = 4/(2 × 10) = 0.2.
questions.explanation: Friction's work is negative; the magnitude gives f and hence μ. W = −100 J, f = 4 N, μ = 0.2.

questions.body: A pendulum bob of mass 0.5 kg on a string of length 1 m is released from the horizontal position. Taking g = 10 m/s², find its speed at the lowest point and the tension in the string there.
questions.rubric: 2 marks: energy conservation ½mv² = mgL → v = √(2gL) ≈ 4.47 m/s. 3 marks: T − mg = mv²/L → T = 15 N.
questions.sampleAnswer: Energy: ½mv² = mgL → v = √(2 × 10 × 1) = √20 ≈ 4.47 m/s. At the lowest point the net upward force is centripetal: T − mg = mv²/L → T = 0.5 × 10 + 0.5 × 20/1 = 5 + 10 = 15 N.
questions.explanation: Tension at the bottom is 3mg for a bob released from the horizontal. v ≈ 4.47 m/s, T = 15 N.

questions.body: A 2 kg block slides from rest down a smooth track of height 5 m and then compresses a spring of force constant 200 N/m on a smooth horizontal floor. Taking g = 10 m/s², find the maximum compression of the spring.
questions.rubric: 3 marks: PE at the top = mgh = 100 J. 3 marks: all of it converts to spring PE, ½kx². 3 marks: x = 1 m. 1 mark: states the track is smooth so no energy is lost.
questions.sampleAnswer: mgh = 2 × 10 × 5 = 100 J. Everything is smooth, so at maximum compression all of it is stored in the spring: ½kx² = 100 → ½ × 200 × x² = 100 → x² = 1 → x = 1 m.
questions.explanation: At maximum compression the block is momentarily at rest, so KE = 0. x = 1 m.

questions.body: A 50 kg girl wearing high heel shoes balances on a single heel. The heel is circular with a diameter of 1.0 cm. What is the pressure exerted by the heel on the horizontal floor? (Take g = 9.8 m/s²)
questions.rubric: 1 mark: radius = 0.005 m. 1 mark: area = πr² = 7.85 × 10⁻⁵ m². 1 mark: thrust = mg = 490 N. 2 marks: P = F/A = 6.24 × 10⁶ N/m².
questions.explanation: Converting the diameter to a radius in metres is where most marks are lost. P = 6.24 × 10⁶ Pa.

answerSheets.note: Complete correct solution ending at 6.24 × 10⁶ N/m².
Right numbers throughout, but the final line writes P = force × area instead of force/area.

questions.body: A rectangular block of mass 40 kg has a base measuring 50 cm × 20 cm. Taking g = 10 m/s², find the pressure it exerts when resting on that base, and state what happens to the pressure if it is stood on a face of half that area.
questions.rubric: 2 marks: area = 0.1 m². 2 marks: P = 400/0.1 = 4000 Pa. 1 mark: halving the area doubles the pressure to 8000 Pa.
questions.sampleAnswer: A = 0.5 × 0.2 = 0.1 m². F = mg = 400 N. P = 400/0.1 = 4000 Pa. Pressure is inversely proportional to area, so on half the area it doubles to 8000 Pa.
questions.explanation: Same thrust, smaller area, larger pressure. 4000 Pa, then 8000 Pa.
